source.title: Interpreting Learned Feedback Patterns in Large Language Models
source.authors: Luke Marks; Amir Abdullah; Clement Neo; Rauno Arike; David Krueger; P. Torr; Fazl Barez

page_placements.theme: Task and reward signals in sparse dictionaries

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses sparse autoencoders to obtain condensed representations for studying learned feedback patterns, and cites superposition as motivation. It does not test whether superposition occurs, whether SAE features recover the model's underlying features, or the geometry or capacity claims in the versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports ablations and activation frequencies for SAE-derived features related to its feedback task. These results concern the task relevance of those features, not whether they are recovered underlying features or evidence for superposition, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. Other reported probe accuracies and correlations measure feedback prediction, not the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAEs on MLP activations of RLHF-tuned models as a tool to build probe inputs for learned feedback patterns, citing superposition as motivation. Its results (probe accuracy, Kendall tau, GPT-4 feature labels, ablation reward, activation frequency) concern feedback prediction and the task relevance of chosen SAE features. None measures feature overlap, capacity, polysemanticity causes, SAE recovery fidelity, or feature dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that probes on SAE-condensed activations of 5 MLP layers recover significant feedback information. This holds strongly for Pythia-160m (tau p=0.014) and for the DPO logistic probes (≥99.8%). GPT-4-flagged features correlate with probe-predicted positive feedback, and ablating them lowers or keeps task reward. The limitations note that SAE features may be compositions or absent from raw activations, though the authors say this does not undermine their main claims.
record.recipe_differences: Rather than testing toy networks for superposition, the study fine-tunes language models, trains sparse autoencoders on selected MLP activations, and probes feedback patterns. It uses SAE features as an interpretability tool.
record.method_sensitivity: not stated for the claim versions; the study selects the five highest parameter-divergence MLP layers for its SAE analysis.

fits_no_version.finding: Zero-ablating GPT-4-flagged SAE features lowered VADER reward for Pythia-70m (2.07 to 1.96) and Pythia-160m (1.95 to 1.69). It left GPT-Neo-125m unchanged at 1.43.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features labelled task-relevant by an LLM can causally affect fine-tuning task performance, with effects varying by model.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-4-flagged features were active on 13.9 to 19.7% of strong-positive-delta inputs, versus 4.1 to 9.1% for the average feature.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM-labelled task-relevant SAE features co-occur with probe-predicted strong feedback more than average features.

record.problems: No direct test of superposition or feature geometry. The paper notes that SAE features may be compositions or may not be present in raw activations, and the reported feature-ablation evidence is limited to the VADER task and three models.
record.rows_left_out: Probe accuracy, reward-prediction correlations, and sentiment-sign results were omitted because they measure feedback prediction rather than any claim version or the relevance of SAE-derived features themselves.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
All: no capacity or importance analysis of neurons.
All: no analysis of polysemanticity's origins.
Whether features are spread across neurons or recoverable by SAEs; SAEs are used but recovery is not checked against ground truth.
Completeness, stability, canonicality of SAE features; the n vs 2n dictionary overlap is used only as a selection filter, and no overlap rate is reported.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T4 and uses_without_test calls are correct. Appendix F's tied-versus-untied and layer-choice SAE loss tables are SAE training diagnostics, not claim tests. The superposition description in the background section is cited only.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model feature overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
Whether real-model features spread across neurons or whether SAE dictionaries recover underlying sparse features. The paper uses SAE representations but does not establish their recovery fidelity.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units. The limitations section notes that SAE features may be compositions or absent from raw activations, but does not test this claim.
Whether the represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study relies on SAE-based feature extraction motivated by superposition and evaluates feedback prediction and task reward, without independently testing a claim version.

tranche.reason: SAEs supply condensed activations for feedback probes. The ablations evaluate selected features' task relevance; they do not test superposition or dictionary completeness, stability or canonicality.

source_check.notes: Table 6 reports before/after rewards without uncertainty or matched control ablations. Section 5.1 acknowledges that SAE features may be compositions or absent from raw activations, citing prior work rather than establishing this experimentally.
